Method of Attack: Uses malicious Excel (.xls) attachments with macros that prompt users to 'Enable Content' to run malicious macros
Uses fake Windows Defender Antivirus themed document templates to trick users into enabling macros
Downloads and installs malware (Emotet) after macro execution
Steals bank credentials, Windows domain credentials, and provides remote access
Installs ransomware (ProLock) once network access is gained
Attack Vector: Spam emails with malicious Excel attachments
Phishing campaigns using fake invoices, payment and banking information, scanned documents
Malware infection via Emotet botnet spam
Indicators of Compromise: Fake Windows Defender Antivirus alert templates
Prompt to 'Enable Content' or 'Enable Editing' in Excel
Installation of Emotet malware following macro execution
